extracted.intended_audience: reviewers, authors, trainees, and editors in the neuroscience journal community (JNeurosci)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and practices for producing and maintaining high-quality peer review at a research journal (The Journal of Neuroscience), including reviewer selection, mentoring, editorial oversight, and acceptable review conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous peer review improves the scientific literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should perform rigorous peer review that improves the scientific literature by catching missed controls, offering different perspectives on interpreting findings, and sometimes identifying fatal flaws that require further experimentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editorial states that rigorous reviews can catch missed controls, interpret findings from a more distant perspective, or reveal fatal flaws that send authors back to the bench; such interventions enhance the reliability and longevity of published work.

rubrics_metrics.name: High standard of scientific rigor and lasting impact for publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers should be held to a high standard of rigor and have lasting impact so that trainees and senior researchers can rely on and cite them confidently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: JNeurosci's goal is to publish work that remains useful many years after publication and to be a trusted source for both recent and archival neuroscience research; reviewers and editors should evaluate manuscripts with these long-term standards in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two levels of editorial oversight (Reviewing Editor and Senior Editor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each paper receives oversight from a Reviewing Editor close to the paper's subject area and a Senior Editor who calibrates standards across areas to ensure consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewing Editors invite knowledgeable reviewers and evaluate reviews and the research; Senior Editors compare decisions across neuroscience domains to make sure standards of review are applied similarly—this procedural design is presented as a quality-control rubric for the editorial process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of consultation sessions to resolve discrepant reviewer opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewers disagree, editors facilitate consultation sessions between discrepant reviewers to reach a consensus set of recommendations for authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedure is explicitly presented as a newly introduced practice at JNeurosci to strengthen review quality by producing a reconciled, actionable set of recommendations rather than leaving authors with conflicting guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared standards for experimental design and statistical analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors and reviewers should work from a common set of standards for experimental design and statistical analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: JNeurosci links to a collection of standards for experimental design and statistical analyses so that reviewers and authors have an explicit reference framework; reviewers are expected to apply these standards when evaluating methods and analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer mentoring and training (constructive and rigorous review)
rubrics_metrics.description: New reviewers (trainees) are trained through a mentoring program to learn what constitutes a constructive and rigorous scientific review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program steps: study provided materials (including neuronline 'How to Peer Review' guidance), pair with an experienced reviewer mentor, jointly review a bioRxiv paper, and graduate only after the mentor agrees the review is strong; trainees must be SfN members and have published at least one manuscript as first author and ideally have experienced peer review themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of mentors and reviewers based on consistent outstanding reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentors and reviewers chosen for mentoring roles are experienced individuals who have consistently provided outstanding reviews for JNeurosci or eNeuro.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most mentors are current editorial-board members; editors use historical performance (consistent quality reviews) to identify who should mentor trainees and serve as reliable reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collegial, respectful tone — zero tolerance for abusive comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews must be collegial and respectful; belittling or degrading comments are not tolerated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors are aware of reviewer identities, screen for inappropriate comments, and rate reviews. If rude or abusive comments appear, editors will ask reviewers to edit them and, in egregious cases, revoke the review and blacklist the reviewer. The policy emphasizes maintaining respectful conversation and that such punitive actions are rare but possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability and performance tracking of reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors track and rate reviewer performance in a reviewer database to ensure accountability and to inform decisions such as mentor selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editorial notes that reviewers are not fully anonymous to editors and that reviews are rated—this tracking underpins quality-control measures and selection for roles like mentorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness, reliability, and helpfulness (practical contributions recognized)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers who are timely, step in for late reviewers, resolve scientific disagreements, or provide consistently outstanding reviews are especially valued and publicly thanked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognition by Reviewing Editors for individuals who fill in for late reviewers, resolve disagreements, or consistently provide high-quality reviews signals that timeliness, problem-solving, and reliability are explicit criteria for what constitutes an exemplary reviewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of external instructional resources on how to peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Trainees and reviewers should consult established instructional materials (e.g., neuronline 'Tricks of the Trade: How to Peer Review a Manuscript') to learn components of constructive reviewing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mentoring program requires trainees to review such materials as a first step so that mentor-trainee work proceeds from shared expectations about what makes a good review.
